chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what do you say regarding chess?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who moves it is like the one who moves the flesh of the pig.' So I said, 'And what is upon the one who moves the flesh of the pig?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He washes his hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia juristic ruling on playing chess according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs a striking juristic analogy, equating the player of chess to one who handles pork, thereby linking the game to ritual impurity (najāsah). The specific instruction to wash the hand suggests that while the act may not render the player permanently impure, it carries a degree of ritual defilement requiring purification, reflecting the early Shia scholarly view of chess as a distraction from spiritual mindfulness.
